evidence: From Cone Saddle, the track climbs steadily to Mount Cone, gaining around 500 m in elevation.
To go to Totara Flats Hut, take the right hand track that continues straight ahead along the ridge.
The track emerges onto a river terrace not far upstream from Totara Flats Hut.
The hut is a few minutes downstream from the bridge.

doubts: The page describes several tracks as separate sections with their own headings, so it is a network. W1 is marked main only because it comes first and runs from the road end. W2 is the Cone Hut descent offered at the junction halfway to Cone Saddle; it has no time or distance of its own. W3 and W4 are the Cone Ridge legs, each with its own heading. The Cone Saddle to Cone Hut or Waiohine Valley tracks are described on the Holdsworth-Kaitoke Track page, so they are not walked here. The Waiohine Road End has no road-end feature in the packet, so the starts have null refs. The Cone Saddle junction before Cone is recorded as a junction without a name. The Tauwharenīkau River is followed on W4 but is not in the names list, so its ref is null. Neill Creek is recorded as a ford because the text says it is crossed twice without a bridge. The huts list includes Cone Hut, which is the end of W2, and Totara Flats and Neill Forks, the ends of W3 and W4; the main way W1 passes no hut. The page does not give times for W2 or W3.
